answer: Each new agent identity must complete a sequential delay proof called a jetty before its votes count: the proof takes a fixed CPU-seconds per epoch and cannot be parallelized. An attacker spinning N identities therefore spends N times the compute every epoch. Honest agents complete one jetty and dock in a shared haven where their completed proofs are recorded in a public atlas, so the cost is asymmetric—only the attacker multiplies the work while a single honest agent pays once.
